notes:
Upstream-clone debugging task on duckdb/duckdb at parent commit 9c21294d984dfe9a1da5d055b5fce3e8a0d634b2 (real upstream issue #25299, fixed upstream by commit c306b47b18095823f22774a972e7cda1170f87a0). PreparedStatement::MissingValuesException in src/include/duckdb/main/prepared_statement.hpp collects the names of parameters not supplied to an EXECUTE into an identifier_set_t (std unordered_set) and joins them in hash-bucket iteration order, so the error 'Values were not provided for the following parameters: ...' lists names in an order unrelated to the statement (observed at parent: ee, cc, dd for a statement declaring aa,bb,cc,dd,ee and supplying aa,bb). The upstream fix collects (declaration-index, name) pairs and sorts by index before building the message; it touches the header only. The image clones the repo at the parent via git init + single shallow fetch so the fix commit is unreachable (rev-list --all --count == 1), overlays the fix-commit regression test (test/sql/prepared/prepared_named_param.test, sha 14da4c35...) into the tree so it fails inside the image with the mined symptom (the q03 block expects 'cc, dd, ee', the buggy engine prints 'ee, cc, dd'), and prebuilds the release engine + unittest runner with the pinned build recipe (cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -j24) so the agent's fix cycle is an incremental header recompile + relink (measured ~16 min at one CPU: 169 objects). Verified both directions inside the task image (see report): at parent the reproduction prints 'ee, cc, dd' and the golden test fails; after the fix it prints 'cc, dd, ee' and the golden test plus the whole test/sql/prepared/* suite (40 sqllogictest cases, 1651 assertions) pass. Hidden cases are CLI-driven inputs the upstream test does not use: 7-name fruit set with middle gaps, t1..t7 with two supply sets, an empty supply on x1..x7, repeated declaration names (b,a,c,b,...), a more-than-3 missing set (p1..p8), and an all-supplied success sanity check asserting the values come back in declaration order; six of the nine hidden queries provably fail at the parent binary (hash order) and all nine pass with the fix. The verifier asserts tree provenance (HEAD == parent, exactly one commit, fix commit absent, only the header fix and the byte-identical golden overlay differ from the pinned commit, /app/explanation.md present and on-topic), rebuilds with ninja -j1, requires the project's own unittest runner to pass the golden test and the prepared suite, requires the CLI reproduction to print the declared order, and runs the hidden cases with exact error-text assertions. Difficulty medium: the fix is a one-file header change but requires locating the message in a real C++ codebase, rebuilding, and reasoning about hash-vs-declaration order. Environment: bench-base:ubuntu-24.04, apt g++/gcc/make/cmake/ninja-build/python3/git, cpus=1, OMP numeric pins, no dependency pins beyond the image ({}).
Review hardening (capstan-longshore review): verifier now removes build/release/duckdb and build/release/test/unittest before its ninja rebuild and requires both to be ELF executables afterwards (kills wrapper/fake binaries that would let the checks pass with the bug still in the sources); verifier timeout_sec raised 1800 -> 3000 to cover the measured ~978s one-CPU incremental rebuild with 3x margin; instruction wording tightened: dropped the explicit 'hash representation' root-cause hint and fixed the duplicate-name promise to match the actually observable contract (supplying a repeated name satisfies every occurrence, so it is absent from the error).
